text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The military-dominated National Security Council (MGK), gathering for a regular monthly meeting on Monday, is expected to cover Syrian-linked guerrilla activities in the southert province of Hatay.
- Thousands of Turks chant slogans supporting secularism at a ceremony held to mark the opening of the 14th Ankara Music Festival.
- The minister of industry says the government cannot dispel the rising Islamist-secularist tension and that a broad-based government should be formed.
- A famous jeweller in the western city of Izmir has been shot dead in his villa.

- An extreme right group close to the Nationalist Action Party has been collecting money for Turkic peoples in Central Asian republics but the money is being deposited in the personal accounts of the group leaders and its use is not monitored.

- Leftist MP Sema Piskinsut, who is in the parlaimantery commission investigating alleged ties of the state with the underworld, says she is worried about the reliability of the commission's report one week ahead of its presentation to parliament.
- A new economic stability programme prepared by the State Planning Department shows similarities to a model used in Argentina in 1991.
- A state minister accompanied by a delegation of 13 went to Iraq to study new trading possibilities following the lifting of the United Nation emborgo in 1996.
